diagram_math_checks.justification: M=ran(T) with the inherited norm; A:X→M, Ax=Tx is the corestriction of the injective T:X→Y, hence bijective. R:M→X is its inverse and is bounded by proof step 1.2 under the equivalent hypotheses. i:M→Y is inclusion. P:Y→Y is the bounded projection from steps 2.1/2.2, and Q:Y→M is its corestriction.

Diagram arrows are X→M labeled A, M→X labeled R, M→Y labeled i, Y→M labeled Q, X→Y labeled T=iA, and Y→X labeled S=RQ. None asserts T or i is onto Y. Native output independently shows all six arrows and those directions.

The definition R(Tx)=x in step 1.2 gives RA=I_X and AR=I_M. For m in M, step 2.1 gives Pm=m, so Qi=I_M for any such projection (also follows from P²=P and ran(P)=M). Therefore ST=RQiA=RA=I_X and TS=iARQ=iQ=P. All composite domains match.

For a left inverse S, step 2.1 gives P=TS=iAS, so Q=AS and RQ=RAS=S. For a given projection P, step 2.2 constructs S=RQ. Thus the single diagram describes either direction without imposing an extra hypothesis. P²=iQiQ=iQ=P follows from Qi=I_M.
The original five numbered proof steps are preserved exactly; Remarks explicitly says the proof is independent of the illustration.
